name: Business Layer
description: Describes what the organization does independently of the software that supports it: business actors and roles, collaborations and interfaces, processes, functions, interactions and events, business services and business objects, and the business capabilities the organization has (ArchiMate 3.2 business layer, with the strategy layer's Capability). Elements here are realized by application services and consume no implementation detail. Modelling rules: actors fill roles, and roles and collaborations are assigned to the processes, functions and interactions they perform (assigned-to); behaviour is never assigned to an actor directly. Internal behaviour realizes business services, which interfaces offer (assigned-to) and which serve actors, roles and processes. Only behaviour accesses business objects and contracts; actors, roles and interfaces reach information through the behaviour assigned to them. Events trigger processes and interactions, and behaviour raises events (triggers); a hand-off between behaviours is flows-to, and a function, having no start, is reached by flows rather than triggered. A business capability is an ability the organization has: business functions and processes realize it, capabilities aggregate narrower capabilities, and software capabilities (product layer) contribute by realizing the business functions behind it. Business services and business capabilities carry the main link to motivation: services realize goals and outcomes, satisfy requirements and deliver value; capabilities support goals and realize outcomes; processes may also realize outcomes and satisfy requirements.
